q: What is the youngest age at which an Illinois teen can get an instruction permit?
exp: Teens aged 15 to 17 can get an instruction permit once they are enrolled in an approved driver education course.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 16

q: What is the minimum number of questions on the Illinois Class D written exam?
exp: Secretary of State rules set the Class D written exam at a minimum of 35 questions.
src: 92 Ill. Adm. Code 1030.80(b)

q: What score do you need to pass the Illinois Class D written exam?
exp: You must answer 80 percent of the questions correctly, which is 28 of 35.
src: 92 Ill. Adm. Code 1030.80(b)

q: How long must a driver under 18 hold an Illinois instruction permit before getting a license?
exp: Drivers aged 15 to 17 must hold the permit for at least nine consecutive months.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), pp. 16, 18; 625 ILCS 5/6-107(b)(1)

q: How many hours of supervised practice must an Illinois driver under 18 complete before getting a license?
exp: Illinois requires at least 50 hours of supervised driving, 10 of them at night, in addition to driver education.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 16; 625 ILCS 5/6-107(b)(3)

q: Who may supervise an Illinois permit holder outside of driver education lessons?
b: Any licensed driver 19 or older in the back seat
c: A parent, guardian or responsible adult 21 or older with a valid license and at least one year of driving experience
d: A licensed driver 21 or older with at least five years of experience
exp: The supervisor must be 21 or older, hold a valid license, have at least one year of driving experience and sit in the front passenger seat.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 16

q: On a Friday night, when does the nighttime driving restriction begin for an Illinois driver under 18?
exp: On Friday and Saturday the restriction runs from 11 p.m. to 6 a.m.; Sunday through Thursday it starts at 10 p.m.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 18

q: During the first 12 months of an Illinois initial license (or until 18), how many passengers under 20 may ride with the teen driver, not counting family members such as siblings?
exp: The driver may carry only one passenger under 20 unless the passengers are siblings, stepsiblings, children or stepchildren.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 18; 625 ILCS 5/6-107(g)

q: An Illinois driver who is 18 wants to talk on the phone with a hands-free device while driving. Is it allowed?
b: No; drivers under 19 may not use a phone at all, except for emergencies
d: Yes, if a licensed adult is in the car
exp: Any phone use while driving, including hands-free, is banned for drivers under 19 except to contact police, a health care provider or emergency services.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), pp. 18 to 19, 22

q: An Illinois resident who is 19, has never been licensed and never took driver education wants a license. What must they complete first?
c: A 6-hour Adult Driver Education Course from a certified provider
exp: First-time applicants aged 18 to 20 without driver education must complete the 6-hour Adult Driver Education Course.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), pp. 4, 18

q: What class of Illinois license do you need to drive an ordinary car?
exp: The basic car license in Illinois is Class D.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 4

q: How many hours of classroom study does an approved Illinois driver education course include?
exp: Approved courses include at least 30 hours in the classroom and 6 hours behind the wheel.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 16

q: How many hours of behind-the-wheel training does an approved Illinois driver education course include?
exp: Approved courses include at least 6 hours of behind-the-wheel training.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 16

q: At what age can an Illinois applicant get an instruction permit without enrolling in driver education?
exp: From 17 years and 3 months you may apply for a permit without taking driver education.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 16

q: How long is an Illinois instruction permit valid?
exp: The instruction permit is valid for 24 months.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 16

q: What is the earliest age at which an Illinois teen can get a driver's license?
exp: You must be at least 16 to get an Illinois driver's license.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 4

q: Where must the supervising adult sit when an Illinois permit holder practices?
d: In the back seat on the right
exp: The supervisor must sit in the front passenger seat next to the driver.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 16

q: During the permit phase, how many passengers may ride in the front seat with an Illinois permit holder?
d: As many as there are belts
exp: Permit holders may carry one front seat passenger, and back seat passengers are limited to the number of belts.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 18; 625 ILCS 5/6-107(e)

q: On a Tuesday, during which hours may an Illinois driver under 18 not drive?
exp: Sunday through Thursday, the nighttime restriction runs from 10 p.m. to 6 a.m.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 18

q: What must an Illinois permit holder avoid during the 9-month permit phase to move on to a license?
a: Any driving infraction, underage alcohol conviction or court supervision
d: Driving more than 20 hours a month
exp: The permit phase must be free of driving infractions, underage alcohol convictions and court supervisions.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 18

q: What happens if an Illinois teen with an initial license gets a traffic conviction in the six months before turning 18?
a: The license is canceled for one year
b: The licensing restrictions can extend past age 18
c: Nothing, if the fine is paid
d: The teen must retake driver education
exp: You must have six conviction-free months before 18, or the restrictions can continue past 18.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 18

q: An Illinois driver under 21 is convicted of two moving violations within 24 months. What is the minimum penalty?
exp: Two or more moving violations within 24 months bring at least a 30-day suspension for drivers under 21.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 20

q: Who can cancel an Illinois license held by a 17-year-old, at any time and for any reason?
d: The parent or guardian who gave consent
exp: The parent or legal guardian who consented may cancel the minor's license until the driver turns 18.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 19

q: What is the minimum visual acuity for an Illinois driver's license, with or without glasses?
exp: Applicants need 20/40 acuity with or without corrective lenses.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 13

q: An Illinois applicant's vision measures between 20/41 and 20/70. What kind of license can they get?
a: A full license with no limits
d: A license limited to 35 mph roads
exp: Acuity between 20/41 and 20/70 limits the driver to daylight driving only.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 13

q: How much side (peripheral) vision do you need for an Illinois license?
exp: Illinois requires at least 140 degrees of peripheral vision.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 13

q: How many attempts does your Illinois application fee cover for the exams?
exp: You are allowed three attempts to pass each exam within one year of paying the application fee.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 13; 92 Ill. Adm. Code 1030.86

q: What happens to an applicant caught cheating on the Illinois written exam?
a: They fail and cannot retake it for 30 days
c: They must retake it the same day
d: They are warned once and may continue
exp: Cheating fails the exam and bars a retake for 30 days.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 13; 92 Ill. Adm. Code 1030.80(k)

q: How much is the fee for an Illinois instruction permit?
exp: The instruction permit fee is $20.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 11

q: How much is an Illinois driver's license for an adult aged 21 to 68?
exp: A driver's license for ages 21 to 68 costs $30.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 11

q: How many documents proving Illinois residency must a first-time REAL ID applicant bring?
exp: A first-time REAL ID applicant brings two residency documents; a standard license needs one.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), pp. 6 to 7

q: Under the REAL ID rules now in force, what does a standard (non REAL ID) Illinois license NOT allow you to do?
c: Prove your age at a store
exp: A standard card is valid for driving and general ID, but not for boarding domestic flights or entering secure federal facilities.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), inside cover

q: What replaced the Illinois Temporary Visitor Driver's License (TVDL)?
exp: TVDLs are no longer issued; people eligible for one can apply for a standard license.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 4; HB 3882 (2023)

q: Which of these tasks is scored on the Illinois driving exam?
b: A three-point turn in a 20-foot space
c: A turnabout using an alley on the left
d: Driving on an interstate at 70 mph
exp: The exam includes a turnabout: signal left, pull into an alley, back out and stay on your side.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 15

q: About how far must you back up on the Illinois driving exam?
exp: You back about 50 feet, slowly and straight, while looking to the rear.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 15

q: During the Illinois driving exam, what happens if you commit a traffic violation?
exp: Any traffic violation or dangerous action during the exam is an automatic fail.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 14; 92 Ill. Adm. Code 1030.85(h)

q: Who may ride in the car with you during the Illinois driving exam?
exp: Only the examiner may be with you during the driving exam.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 14

q: Under the Illinois Cooperative Driver Testing Program, what grade must a student earn in driver education to skip the facility driving exam?
c: A combined grade of A or B
d: A grade of C or better
exp: Students who finish an accredited course with a combined A or B may be exempt from the facility driving exam.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 17

q: A new resident moves to Illinois with a valid license from another state. How long can they drive on it?
c: Until it expires, however long that is
d: Until they get an Illinois license, within 90 days or before it expires, whichever comes first
exp: New residents must get an Illinois license within 90 days or before the old license expires, whichever comes first.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 5

q: Under 18, which document must you bring when you apply for your Illinois driver's license?
a: Your 50-hour driving log with the proper signature
c: A letter from your school principal
exp: Teens bring the permit, ID documents, consent or certificate if needed, and the signed 50-hour log.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 16

q: How many points can you lose on the Illinois Class D driving exam and still pass?
exp: Class C and D applicants are allowed 36 points; immediate disqualification still applies for violations and dangerous actions.
src: 92 Ill. Adm. Code 1030.85(g)

q: What does an eight-sided red sign mean?
b: Stop only if traffic is coming
exp: The octagon is used only for stop signs.
src: core Chapter 2; FHWA MUTCD 11th ed. 2B

q: What does a downward pointing triangle with a red border tell you?
a: Stop and wait for a green light
exp: The downward triangle is the yield sign: slow down and let traffic with the right of way go first.
src: core Chapter 2; FHWA MUTCD 11th ed. 2B

q: A round yellow sign with a black X and the letters RR means what?
d: You are at the railroad crossing itself
exp: The round yellow sign is the railroad advance warning sign, placed before the tracks.
src: core Chapter 2; FHWA MUTCD 11th ed. 8B

q: Where is the yellow pennant shaped No Passing Zone sign placed?
a: On the right side of the road
b: On the left side of the road
exp: The pennant stands on the left, where you look before pulling out to pass.
src: core Chapter 2; FHWA MUTCD 11th ed. 2C

q: What does a five-sided sign shaped like a house warn you about?
c: A school zone or school crossing
exp: The pentagon shape is used only for school signs.
src: core Chapter 2; FHWA MUTCD 11th ed. 7B

q: What color are signs that warn of road work?
exp: Orange marks temporary traffic control in work zones.
src: core Chapter 2; FHWA MUTCD 11th ed. 6F

q: What does a fluorescent pink sign reading INCIDENT AHEAD mean?
a: A crash or emergency scene is ahead
exp: Fluorescent pink marks incident management areas.
src: core Chapter 2; FHWA MUTCD 11th ed. 6N

q: What is the usual shape and color of a warning sign?
exp: Most warning signs are yellow diamonds with black symbols or words.
src: core Chapter 2; FHWA MUTCD 11th ed. 2C

q: A blue sign along the highway shows what kind of information?
c: Services such as gas, food and lodging
exp: Blue signs point to motorist services.
src: core Chapter 2; FHWA MUTCD 11th ed. 2I

q: A brown sign points you toward what?
d: A park, recreation area or historic site
exp: Brown guide signs mark recreation and cultural sites.
src: core Chapter 2; FHWA MUTCD 11th ed. 2H

q: What does a white rectangular sign with black letters usually show?
a: A traffic rule you must obey
exp: White rectangles with black letters are regulatory signs that state a law.
src: core Chapter 2; FHWA MUTCD 11th ed. 2B

q: You see a red sign that says WRONG WAY facing you. What does it mean?
a: The road ahead is closed for repairs
b: You are driving against traffic and must turn around safely
c: You must exit at the next ramp
exp: A Wrong Way sign facing you means you entered against the flow of traffic.
src: core Chapter 2; FHWA MUTCD 11th ed. 2B

q: A square yellow plaque reading 30 MPH is below a curve sign. What does it mean?
a: 30 mph is the new legal speed limit
b: You must drive at least 30 mph
c: 30 mph is the advised top speed for the curve
exp: The yellow plaque is an advisory speed for the curve, not the legal limit.
src: core Chapter 2; FHWA MUTCD 11th ed. 2C

q: What does a Lane Ends sign tell you?
a: Traffic from another road will join yours
c: Your road ends at a T intersection
d: One lane is ending and its traffic must merge
exp: Lane Ends means a lane is about to end, so drivers in it must merge.
src: core Chapter 2; FHWA MUTCD 11th ed. 2C

q: What does a Divided Highway Ends sign warn you about?
a: Oncoming traffic will soon be next to you with no median
b: A median will soon split the road
c: The highway ends at a stop sign
exp: When the median ends, traffic moves in both directions with no divider.
src: core Chapter 2; FHWA MUTCD 11th ed. 2C

q: In a work zone, a flagger turns the paddle so SLOW faces you. What should you do?
b: Proceed slowly and watch for workers
c: Speed up to clear the zone
exp: SLOW means move ahead slowly and carefully through the work area.
src: core Chapter 2; FHWA MUTCD 11th ed. 6E

q: A lighted arrow board in a work zone flashes an arrow pointing right. What should you do?
b: Turn right at the next street
d: Stay in your lane and speed up
exp: A flashing arrow means the lane ahead is closed; merge the way the arrow points.
src: core Chapter 2; FHWA MUTCD 11th ed. 6L

q: On a barricade, diagonal stripes slope down toward the right. Which way should you pass?
c: Stop and wait for a flagger
exp: Stripes slope down toward the side on which traffic should pass.
src: core Chapter 2; FHWA MUTCD 11th ed. 6K

q: An Interstate route has an odd number, such as 55. Which way does it usually run?
c: In a loop around a city
exp: Odd numbered Interstates run mostly north and south.
src: core Chapter 2; FHWA MUTCD 11th ed. 2D

q: Under what conditions does the 20 mph Illinois school zone limit apply?
a: Every day from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m.
b: On school days from 6:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. when children are present and signs are posted
c: Only when a police officer is present
d: On school days from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m., whether or not children are present
exp: The 20 mph limit applies on school days between 6:30 a.m. and 4 p.m. when children are present and signs are posted.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), pp. 24 to 25

q: What is the speed limit in a marked Illinois school zone while the limit is in effect?
exp: Drivers must slow to 20 mph in a marked school zone while the limit is in effect.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), pp. 24 to 25

q: When must you obey the posted speed limit in an Illinois construction zone?
d: 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, whether or not workers are present
exp: The work zone limit applies at all times, regardless of whether workers are there.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 25

q: In an Illinois construction zone, may you pass another vehicle?
a: No; all Illinois construction zones are no passing zones
b: Yes, if the road has two lanes
c: Yes, if no workers are present
exp: Every construction zone in Illinois is a no passing zone.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 29

q: What does Illinois law require you to do with your phone when entering a work zone?
b: Stop using it unless it is in hands-free mode
d: Nothing; work zones have no phone rule
exp: Drivers must stop wireless phone use in work zones unless using a hands-free device.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 25

q: In Illinois, what can happen after a second conviction for speeding in a construction zone within two years when workers were present?
c: Your driver's license can be suspended
d: You must retake the written exam
exp: A second work zone speeding violation within two years with workers present is grounds for suspension.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 60; 625 ILCS 5/11-605.1(g)

q: In Illinois, you approach a school zone crosswalk on a school day and children are close to it. What must you do?
d: Come to a complete stop and yield
exp: On school days you must stop and yield when children are close to a school zone crosswalk.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 27

q: In Illinois, may you turn right on a steady red light?
b: Yes, without stopping if the way is clear
c: Only when a green arrow is also lit
d: Yes, after a complete stop and yielding, unless a sign forbids it
exp: Right on red is allowed after a full stop and yielding unless a sign prohibits it.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), pp. 26, 77; 625 ILCS 5/11-306(c)(3)

q: In Illinois, when is a left turn on a red light allowed?
a: From a one-way street onto a one-way street with traffic moving left, after stopping
c: From a two-way street onto a one-way street
exp: Left on red is allowed only from a one-way street onto another one-way street whose traffic moves to the left.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), pp. 26, 77; 625 ILCS 5/11-306(c)(3)

q: In Illinois, you face a steady red arrow pointing right and no sign prohibits the turn. What may you do?
b: Turn right after a complete stop and yielding
c: Never turn until the arrow turns green
d: Turn only if a police officer waves you on
exp: The turn-on-red rule applies to any steady red signal, so after a full stop and yield the right turn is allowed.

q: What must you do in Illinois if a traffic signal is completely dark because it is not working?
a: Drive through if no cars are near
b: Treat it as a yield sign
c: Treat the intersection as an all-way stop
exp: When signals are not working, stop as at an all-way stop and yield before entering.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 77

q: Under Illinois's Scott's Law, what should you do when approaching a stationary emergency vehicle with flashing lights on a road with two lanes in your direction?
a: Change to a lane not next to it if safe, or slow down and proceed with caution
b: Speed up to pass it quickly
c: Stop in your lane until it leaves
exp: Move to a lane away from the vehicle when possible; otherwise reduce speed and proceed carefully.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 25; 625 ILCS 5/11-907(c)

q: What is the fine range for a first violation of Illinois's Move Over law (Scott's Law)?
exp: A first violation is a business offense with a fine of $250 to $10,000.

q: On a four-lane Illinois highway, you approach a disabled vehicle with hazard lights on. What does the law require?
a: Nothing, since it is not an emergency vehicle
c: Change lanes away from it if safe; otherwise slow down
exp: Illinois law requires drivers to move away from a disabled vehicle using hazard lights when safe, or slow down.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 45

q: On an Illinois two-lane road, a school bus stops with red lights flashing and stop arm out. Who must stop?
c: No one if no children are visible
exp: On a two-lane road, traffic from either direction must stop.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 33; 625 ILCS 5/11-1414(a)

q: When may Illinois drivers coming from the opposite direction pass a stopped school bus without stopping?
a: On a highway with four or more lanes, at least two in each direction
b: On any road with a center line
d: When the bus is in a school parking lot
exp: Oncoming traffic need not stop on a roadway with at least four lanes, two in each direction.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 32; 625 ILCS 5/11-1414(e)

q: After stopping for an Illinois school bus, when may you go?
a: As soon as the children reach the sidewalk
b: When the stop arm is withdrawn and lights are off, or the bus driver signals you
exp: Stay stopped until the stop arm is no longer out and the lights are off, or the bus driver waves you on.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 33

q: What is the penalty for a first conviction of passing a stopped school bus in Illinois?
c: A 3-month license suspension and a $300 fine
exp: A first conviction brings a 3-month suspension, a mandatory $300 fine and community service.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 33; 625 ILCS 5/11-1414(f)

q: Illinois law sets no exact distance for stopping behind a school bus. What distance does the Illinois State Board of Education advise?
exp: The State Board of Education advises stopping at least 20 feet from the bus.
src: ISBE, Bus Safety for Motorists (isbe.net)

q: Where must Illinois drivers stop for a school bus that is loading or unloading?
a: On any road, private road or school parking lot, unless the four-lane exception applies
b: Only on public roads in towns
exp: The stop rule covers any roadway, private road and school parking lot.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 33

q: In Illinois, you may not turn around on a curve or hill unless you can see how far in all directions?
exp: Do not turn around on curves or hills unless you can see at least 500 feet in all directions.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 32

q: Who may prohibit U-turns on some Illinois roadways?
d: No one; U-turns are always legal
exp: Municipalities may prohibit U-turns on some roads.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 32

q: In an Illinois business or residential area, how far before a turn must you signal?
exp: In business or residential areas, give a continuous signal for at least 100 feet.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 30

q: Outside business and residential areas in Illinois, how far before a turn must you signal?
exp: In other areas, the signal must start at least 200 feet before the turn.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 30

q: In Illinois, is it legal to flash your turn signals to tell the driver behind you it is safe to pass?
b: No, it is against the law
d: Yes, on highways posted above 45 mph
exp: Flashing turn signals as a courtesy or pass signal is illegal in Illinois.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 28

q: Unless posted otherwise, what is the speed limit on Illinois interstates and tollways?
exp: The default limit on interstates and tollways is 70 mph.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 24

q: Unless posted otherwise, what is the speed limit on Illinois highways with four lanes?
exp: Four-lane highways have a default limit of 65 mph.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 24

q: Unless posted otherwise, what is the speed limit in Illinois cities and towns?
exp: The default limit in city and town areas is 30 mph.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 24

q: Unless posted otherwise, what is the speed limit in an Illinois alley?
exp: Alleys have a default limit of 15 mph.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 24

q: Unless posted otherwise, what is the speed limit on other Illinois highways and in rural areas?
exp: Other highways and rural areas default to 55 mph.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 24

q: What does Illinois law say about following distance?
b: Stay at least 100 feet behind at all speeds
c: There is no rule about following distance
d: Do not follow more closely than is reasonable and prudent for speed, traffic and road conditions
exp: The law bans following more closely than is reasonable and prudent; it sets no fixed number.

q: How much following distance does the Illinois manual advise behind a motorcycle?
a: At least three to four seconds
exp: Allow at least three to four seconds so the rider has room to react in an emergency.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 42

q: In the Chicago area, how should you treat reversible express lanes such as those on the Kennedy Expressway?
a: Use them in either direction at any time
c: Enter them anywhere by crossing the barrier
d: Enter only where signs show they are open in your direction
exp: Reversible lanes carry traffic one way at a time, so use them only when signs show they are open your way.
src: IDOT, reported by WTTW News, 2024-12-17 and 2025-01-09 (news.wttw.com)

q: On some Chicago area expressways, Pace buses may drive on the shoulder when traffic is slow. May you drive on the shoulder too?
a: No; never use the shoulder as a travel lane
c: Yes, when traffic is under 35 mph
d: Yes, if you have two passengers
exp: Bus on shoulder is only for Pace buses; passing on the shoulder is not allowed for cars.
src: pacebus.com/i90; Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 28

q: In Illinois, how close to a fire hydrant may you park?
exp: Standing or parking within 15 feet of a fire hydrant is prohibited.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 35

q: In Illinois, you may not park within how many feet of a stop sign, yield sign or traffic signal?
exp: Standing or parking within 30 feet of a stop sign, yield sign or signal is prohibited.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 36

q: In Illinois, you may not park within how many feet of the nearest rail of a railroad crossing?
exp: Parking within 50 feet of the nearest rail is prohibited.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 36

q: In Illinois, you may not park within how many feet of a crosswalk at an intersection?
exp: Standing or parking within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection or a fire station driveway is prohibited.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 36

q: When parallel parking on an Illinois two-way street, how close to the curb must your right wheels be?
exp: Park parallel to and within 12 inches of the curb.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 35

q: In Illinois, you park facing downhill on a street with a curb. Which way do you turn your front wheels?
exp: Facing downhill with a curb, turn the wheels toward the curb so the car rolls into it.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 34

q: How much space must you leave when passing a bicyclist in Illinois?
exp: Illinois requires at least 3 feet of passing space, measured from your side mirror.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), pp. 28, 43; 625 ILCS 5/11-703(d)

q: In Illinois, may you pass a bicyclist in a no-passing zone?
b: Yes, at any time if you honk first
c: Only if the bike is going under half the speed limit, you stay within the limit and there is room to the left
exp: Illinois allows passing a slow bicycle in a no-passing zone only when all of these conditions are met.

q: In Illinois, may you stop briefly in a marked bike lane to drop off a passenger?
b: Yes, if you use your hazard lights
c: Yes, if no bicyclist is in sight
d: No, not even when no bicyclists are present
exp: Drivers may not drive, park, idle or drop off or pick up passengers in bike lanes.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), pp. 35, 42

q: What is the Dutch Reach that the Illinois manual recommends?
a: Opening your car door with the hand farther from it so you turn and check for bikes
b: Signaling a turn with your right arm
c: Reaching for the parking brake before opening the door
d: Holding the steering wheel with one hand when turning
exp: Using the far hand to open the door turns your body so you can see bicyclists coming from behind.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), pp. 30, 43

q: In Illinois, you must report a crash that involves death, injury or property damage over what amount?
exp: A report is required for death, bodily injury or damage over $1,500, regardless of fault.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 54

q: If any vehicle in an Illinois crash is uninsured, a report is required when damage is more than what amount?
exp: With an uninsured vehicle involved, a report is required for damage over $500.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 54

q: According to the Illinois manual, how long does a driver have to report a crash after it occurs?
exp: The Rules of the Road states a driver has 30 minutes to report a crash.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 55

q: You damage a parked car in Illinois and cannot find the owner. What must you do?
a: Drive away if the damage is small
b: Leave your name, address, phone and plate number on it and notify police
c: Wait at the car for 24 hours
exp: Leave your information on the vehicle, notify police and complete any required reports.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 55

q: In Illinois, within what distance of an oncoming vehicle must you dim your high beams?
exp: Switch to low beams when an oncoming vehicle is within 500 feet.

q: In Illinois, when following another vehicle, within what distance must you dim your high beams?
exp: Use low beams when you are within 300 feet behind another vehicle.

q: Failing to report a crash in Illinois can bring what penalty?
a: A fine up to $2,500 and up to one year in jail
exp: Drivers who fail to report a crash may be fined up to $2,500 and jailed up to one year.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 55

q: What is the legal BAC limit for an Illinois driver 21 or older?
exp: It is illegal to drive with a BAC of 0.08 percent or more.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 48

q: What is the alcohol limit for an Illinois driver under 21?
a: Any trace of alcohol is a violation
exp: Under 21, any trace of alcohol while driving brings at least a 3-month suspension.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 52; 625 ILCS 5/11-501.8

q: An Illinois driver under 21 is found with any trace of alcohol while driving. What is the minimum suspension?
exp: Any trace of alcohol suspends a driver under 21 for at least three months.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 52

q: What THC level in whole blood is illegal for Illinois drivers?
exp: Driving with 5 ng/mL or more of THC in whole blood (or 10 ng/mL in other bodily substance) is illegal.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 48

q: A first-time Illinois driver refuses a chemical test after a DUI arrest. How long is the license suspended?
exp: Refusing chemical testing brings a one-year statutory summary suspension for a first offender.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 49

q: A first-time Illinois driver fails a chemical test with a BAC of 0.08 or more. How long is the license suspended?
exp: A test showing 0.08 or more brings a six-month statutory summary suspension.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 49

q: After an Illinois DUI arrest, on which day does the statutory summary suspension begin?
exp: The officer gives a temporary receipt good for 45 days; the suspension starts on day 46.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 49

q: What is the minimum revocation for a first DUI conviction in Illinois for a driver 21 or older?
exp: A first DUI conviction revokes driving privileges for at least one year.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 50

q: What is the minimum revocation for a first DUI conviction for an Illinois driver under 21?
exp: Drivers under 21 convicted of DUI face at least a two-year revocation.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 52

q: How is a first DUI classified in Illinois?
exp: A first DUI conviction is a Class A misdemeanor.

q: Under Illinois law, who may drink alcohol in a moving vehicle?
b: Passengers in a limousine, chartered bus or motor home only
exp: Drinking in a vehicle is illegal, except for passengers in chartered buses, motor homes and limousines.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 51; 625 ILCS 5/11-502(c)

q: Which phone use is allowed for an Illinois driver aged 25 while driving?
c: A call in hands-free or voice-operated mode
d: Scrolling social media at a red light
exp: Drivers 19 and older may use hands-free mode; holding a phone, video and social media are banned.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 22; 625 ILCS 5/12-610.2

q: When may an Illinois driver use a handheld phone in the car?
d: To report an emergency, or when parked on the shoulder
exp: Handheld use is allowed only to report an emergency, while parked on the shoulder, or when stopped by blocked traffic in neutral or park.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 22

q: What is the maximum fine for a first violation of the Illinois handheld phone law?
exp: Fines are up to $75 for a first offense, $100 for a second, $125 for a third and $150 after that.

q: Which headset use is allowed for an Illinois driver 19 or older?
b: A single-sided headset or earpiece with a phone
exp: Headsets are banned, but one earpiece or single-sided headset with a phone is allowed.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 22

q: In Illinois, which vehicle occupants must wear seat belts?
a: Every driver and passenger 8 or older, front and back
exp: All drivers and passengers age 8 and older, in front and back seats, must buckle up.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 23

q: In Illinois, who is responsible for making sure every passenger obeys the seat belt and child seat laws?
c: The vehicle owner if not driving
exp: The driver is responsible for all passengers obeying the belt law and the Child Passenger Protection Act.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 23

q: Under Illinois's Child Passenger Protection Act, which children must ride in a child safety restraint?
exp: Children under 8 must be secured in an appropriate child restraint system.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 23

q: Until what age must an Illinois child ride rear-facing, unless the child weighs more than 40 pounds or is taller than 40 inches?
exp: Children must ride rear-facing until age 2 unless over 40 pounds or 40 inches.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 24

q: An Illinois booster seat must be used with what kind of belt?
exp: Booster seats must be used only with a lap and shoulder belt.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 23

q: What are the minimum liability insurance amounts for an Illinois car?
a: $10,000 per person, $20,000 per crash and $5,000 property damage
b: $25,000 per person, $50,000 per crash and $20,000 property damage
c: $50,000 per person, $100,000 per crash and $40,000 property damage
d: $15,000 per person, $30,000 per crash and $10,000 property damage
exp: Illinois minimum liability coverage is $25,000 per person, $50,000 per crash and $20,000 for property damage.
src: 625 ILCS 5/7-203; HB 66 (104th GA) bill status

q: What is the minimum penalty for an Illinois mandatory insurance conviction?
c: Loss of driving privileges for 3 months
exp: Drivers convicted of mandatory insurance violations lose their privileges for at least three months and pay a $100 reinstatement fee.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 55

q: Besides sunset to sunrise, when must you use headlights in Illinois?
a: Only when you cannot see 500 feet ahead
d: Whenever weather requires your windshield wipers
exp: Headlights are required when rain, snow, fog or other conditions require wipers, and when you cannot see clearly 1,000 feet ahead.

q: In Illinois, a car sound system is illegal if it can be heard how far from the vehicle?
exp: A sound system audible 75 feet or more from a moving vehicle on a highway is illegal.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 36

q: How soon must you tell the Illinois Secretary of State about an address change?
exp: Report an address change within 10 days of any move.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 6

q: On the Illinois driving exam, when must you adjust your seat, safety belt and mirrors?
b: Before the vehicle is put into motion
exp: All adjustments must be made before the vehicle moves.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 14

q: During the backing task on the Illinois driving exam, where should you look?
c: Turn your head to the right and watch to the rear
exp: Back slowly and straight while turning your head right and watching to the rear.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 15

q: Which hill tasks are on the Illinois driving exam?
b: Stopping on a hill and rolling back
d: Parking uphill and downhill and starting from each
exp: You park uphill and downhill at the side of the road and start from both positions.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 15

q: What must the car you bring to the Illinois driving exam have?
a: Valid plates and registration, required equipment and proof of insurance
exp: The car must be properly licensed, equipped and insured, with proof of insurance at the exam.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 14

q: During the Illinois driving exam turnabout, which signal do you use before pulling into the alley on the left?
exp: Turn on your left signal before turning into the alley, then back out and stay on your side.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 15

q: What happens if you make a dangerous move during the Illinois driving exam?
b: The examiner gives you a second try
d: You must finish but cannot retest that day
exp: A dangerous action or any traffic violation is an automatic fail, whatever your point total.
src: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026 (SOS, July 2026), p. 14; 92 Ill. Adm. Code 1030.85(h)

q: An ambulance with its siren on comes up behind you in Illinois. Where does the law tell you to drive?
a: To the left edge of the road, clear of traffic
c: To the right-hand edge or curb, clear of any intersection
d: Nowhere; keep moving at the speed limit
exp: Illinois drivers must pull to a position as close as possible to the right-hand edge or curb, clear of any intersection, and stop if needed.
src: 625 ILCS 5/11-907(a); RR p. 25 (Emergency/Maintenance Vehicles)

q: A fire truck is answering an alarm in Illinois. How close behind it may you follow?
exp: Illinois bans following fire apparatus answering an alarm closer than 500 feet, or stopping within 500 feet of one at a fire.

q: You are stopped at an Illinois intersection with two-way traffic when an emergency vehicle with lights and siren approaches. What should you do?
a: Stay stopped until it has passed through the intersection
b: Drive through the intersection quickly to clear the way
d: Turn right on red to get out of the way
exp: If you are stopped at an intersection with two-way traffic, remain stopped until the emergency vehicle passes through it.
src: RR p. 25 (Emergency/Maintenance Vehicles)

q: May you drive over a fire hose lying across an Illinois street?
b: Yes, if no water is flowing
d: No, unless the fire official in charge allows it
exp: Illinois prohibits driving over fire hoses unless the fire official in command of the scene permits it.
src: RR p. 25 (Emergency/Maintenance Vehicles)

q: A slow car ahead of you is in the left lane of an Illinois highway. May you pass it by driving on the right shoulder?
a: Yes, if the shoulder is paved
c: No, passing off the pavement is not allowed
exp: Illinois does not allow driving off the pavement or main traveled part of the road to pass, on the right or the left.
src: RR p. 28

q: Illinois law requires headlights whenever you cannot clearly see people and vehicles how far ahead?
exp: Headlights are required when, because of poor light or weather, people and vehicles are not clearly visible at 1,000 feet.

q: It is noon in Illinois and light snow makes you run your wipers. What does the law say about headlights?
exp: Illinois requires headlights whenever rain, snow, fog or other weather requires the windshield wipers.

q: An Illinois officer stops you and asks for proof of insurance, which is in your glove box. What should you do first?
a: Reach for it right away so the stop goes faster
b: Tell the officer where it is, then follow the officer's directions
c: Step out of the car and open the passenger door
exp: The manual says to tell the officer the documents are in the glove box, under the seat or on your phone, then follow directions before you reach.
src: RR pp. 21 to 22 (Proper Action When Stopped by Law Enforcement)

q: At night, an unmarked car flashes lights behind you and you cannot tell if it is the police. What does the Illinois manual allow?
b: Stop at once on a bridge
c: Drive slowly to a well lit, busy place or a police station, or call 911
d: Ignore it until it turns on a siren
exp: Drive carefully below the limit and pull over at a well lit, populated place, go to the nearest police station, or call 911.
src: RR pp. 21 to 22 (Proper Action When Stopped by Law Enforcement)

q: An Illinois officer hands you a ticket to sign. What does signing it mean?
a: Only that you received the ticket
c: That you give up your right to court
d: That you agree to pay the fine today
exp: Signing a ticket is not an admission of guilt; it only shows you received it. You can contest it in traffic court.
src: RR pp. 21 to 22 (Proper Action When Stopped by Law Enforcement)

q: Police signal you to stop and you are on a bridge in Illinois. What should you do?
a: Stop right away in your lane
b: Stop next to the bridge wall
c: Back up to the end of the bridge
d: Keep going slowly to the next safe spot, then pull over
exp: Do not stop on bridges, curves, or next to guardrails or walls; find the next safe place to pull over.
src: RR pp. 21 to 22 (Proper Action When Stopped by Law Enforcement)

q: A 19-year-old in Illinois is caught drinking beer at a friend's house. How does Illinois law treat it?
exp: For anyone under 21, buying, accepting, possessing or drinking alcohol is a Class A misdemeanor in Illinois.

q: A 17-year-old receives court supervision for having alcohol while riding as a passenger in a car. What happens to the license in Illinois?
a: Nothing, since the teen was not driving
exp: Court supervision for an underage alcohol offense committed while in a motor vehicle brings a 3-month suspension.

q: An Illinois driver under 21 is convicted of possessing alcohol in a car. What is the minimum suspension?
exp: A conviction for an underage alcohol offense committed while in a motor vehicle brings at least a six-month suspension.

q: A 20-year-old uses an older friend's ID to buy alcohol in Illinois. What is the offense?
a: No offense if the ID was real
b: A petty offense with a $25 fine
d: Only the store is at fault
exp: Under 21, using another person's ID or a false ID to get alcohol is a Class A misdemeanor.

q: How many moving violation convictions within 12 months put an Illinois driver up for a points-based suspension?
exp: Three or more convictions for point-assigned offenses within 12 months lead to a suspension or revocation based on the point total.

q: How many points does Illinois assign for speeding 11 to 14 mph over the limit?
exp: Illinois assigns 5 points for 1 to 10 mph over, 15 for 11 to 14, 20 for 15 to 25 and 50 for 26 or more.
src: 92 Ill. Adm. Code 1040.20

q: An Illinois driver with no suspension in the past seven years has three convictions in 12 months totaling 40 points. What is the suspension?
exp: With no prior suspension in seven years, 15 to 44 points brings a 2-month suspension; 110 or more brings revocation.
src: 92 Ill. Adm. Code 1040.30(a)

q: Under Illinois's point table, what happens at 110 points or more after three or more convictions in 12 months?
exp: 110 or more points brings revocation.
src: 92 Ill. Adm. Code 1040.30
